chapter: Kansas City bands and the Blue Devils
title: Jesse Stone as arranger and bandleader
summary: They liked Jesse Stone because he threw anything on paper; Durham calls him underrated, ten years ahead, and describes him now playing organ with his wife.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: And we liked Jesse because Jesse would throw anything on the paper and we liked that.
Yeah, I was going to say, he was -- as an arranger, he was ahead in those days, wasn't he?
Yeah, he's -- today, Jesse Stone is so underrated.
Yeah, I heard him about two years ago. He's playing with a ______, he and his wife. He's playing a little organ, she's playing a drum, and they go out here
and play. They played holiday and motels a lot. They got some act. Both of them are singing duos and singing.
Yeah. He wrote Hidey-Ho and numbers like that.
You think he's a good piano player or just a sort of arranger's piano --
He's an arranger's piano and also a background man for the band (inaudible) the band.
Oh, yeah. It's surprising that nobody ever gets on him for -- I mean, maybe he should do one of these things, because he must be nearly --
(Inaudible) we play a song every night, Hidey-Ho and -- even Frank Williams got that when was on it. And he did a lot of other songs. Wait a minute. He did Hucka Buck and a lot of other things.
But this band he had was really a very good one at that time, wasn't it?
You were playing trombone in it.
